claim: On 4x CMP 170HX, pipeline parallelism beats tensor parallelism by 6.6x on prefill (5,321 vs 801 tok/s at 77k context) and roughly 2x on aggregate decode.
stance_target: The repo's claim that TP is ruled out by the fabric and that PP is the viable multi-GPU topology
scope_conditions: DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 on 4x CMP 170HX, PCIe Gen2 x4, no P2P, vLLM with the repo's patches
quoted_support: On these cards PP beats TP by 6.6x on prefill (5,321 vs 801 tok/s at 77k context) and roughly 2x on aggregate decode.

claim: Tensor parallel issues 86 collectives per forward pass on this model (2 all-reduces x 43 layers), each moving tokens x hidden bytes.
stance_target: The repo's arithmetic that TP costs two all-reduces per layer and therefore scales badly on a slow fabric
quoted_support: tensor parallel performs 2 all-reduces per layer x 43 layers = 86 collectives per forward, each moving tokens x hidden bytes. Double the tokens and you double both compute and communication, so a communication-bound setup stays communication-bound at every sequence length

claim: Pipeline parallel moves the same payload only 3 times (one hand-off per stage boundary) and overlaps it with compute, about 28x less data on the wire than TP.
stance_target: The repo's claim that PP is the topology that survives a no-P2P PCIe Gen2 x4 fabric
quoted_support: Pipeline parallel moves the same payload only 3 times (one hand-off per stage boundary) and overlaps it with compute: ~28x less data on the wire.

claim: The fabric is PCIe Gen2 x4 with no P2P, measuring about 1.0 GB/s of bus bandwidth, which the author calls close to the worst case for TP.
stance_target: The repo's measured PCIe Gen2 x4 / no-P2P hardware claim
scope_conditions: 4x CMP 170HX in one box, vLLM PP4 deployment
quoted_support: The CMP 170HX is PCIe Gen2 x4 with no P2P (~1.0 GB/s measured bus bandwidth), which is close to the worst case for TP. On a machine with NVLink the trade-off would look completely different.

claim: TP prefill measures flat at ~800 tok/s from 1.5k to 77k tokens, which is the signature of a setup that is communication-bound at every sequence length.
stance_target: The repo's claim that TP cannot be rescued by increasing batch or sequence length on this fabric
scope_conditions: DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 TP4 on 4x CMP 170HX, prefill sweep 1.5k to 77k tokens
quoted_support: which is exactly why TP prefill measures flat at ~800 tok/s from 1.5k to 77k tokens

claim: FP8 KV cache works correctly on sm_80 because the conversion is done in software; only FP8 math requires sm_89 or newer.
stance_target: The repo's claim that GA100 has no FP8 tensor cores but that FP8 storage formats are still usable
scope_conditions: DeepSeek-V4-Flash on sm_80 (GA100), vLLM with --kv-cache-dtype fp8
quoted_support: Effectively required. DeepSeek-V4 asserts fp8_ds_mla layout only supports fp8 kv-cache. FP8 KV does work correctly on sm_80 - the conversion is software; only FP8 math needs sm_89+.

claim: PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True is a hard failure at model load on these cards: it cannot map 20 MB with 28.6 GiB free, suggesting CUDA VMM is broken on GA100 CMP parts.
stance_target: The default assumption that standard PyTorch memory-management mitigations work on this hardware
quoted_support: it is a hard failure at model load on these cards: expandable_segments: memory mapping failed with OOM on device 3 while trying to map 20971520 bytes (free: 28626452480), i.e. it cannot map 20 MB with 28.6 GiB free. CUDA VMM appears broken on GA100 CMP parts.

claim: Retrieval accuracy degrades with context depth regardless of tuning, from ~100% at 150k to ~30% at 900k tokens, and the author calls this architectural rather than a tuning problem.
stance_target: Whether the 1M-token context capability is uniformly usable, which bears on the value of 32k-context CSA2 training
scope_conditions: DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 on 4x CMP 170HX, retrieval probes across depth
quoted_support: None of these settings change retrieval accuracy, which degrades with depth regardless (~100% at 150k -> ~30% at 900k). That is architectural, not a tuning problem.

claim: At 1M context the time-to-first-token is 9.2 minutes and decode drops to about 40 tok/s, so the full window is reachable but not practical.
stance_target: The practical ceiling on long-context work on this box
quoted_support: The only reason not to set the maximum is time, not capacity: TTFT at 1M is 9.2 minutes and decode drops to ~40 tok/s.

claim: Rebalancing the 43 layers as 12,12,12,7 across four pipeline ranks removes an 8.7 GiB rank imbalance and grows the KV pool by ~85%.
stance_target: The claim that pipeline-parallel memory balance, not raw link bandwidth, is the tunable lever on this box
quoted_support: Rebalances the 43 layers off pipeline rank 3, which uniquely carries lm_head and the DSpark drafter. Does not affect the context ceiling - but it removes an 8.7 GiB rank imbalance and grows the KV pool ~85% (798,660 -> 1,476,563 at max-model-len 163840).

claim: --enforce-eager costs roughly 12x throughput (8-10 tok/s versus CUDA-graph execution), so CUDA graphs are mandatory on this hardware.
stance_target: The claim that kernel-launch overhead dominates unless graphs are captured, a constraint any training harness here must respect
scope_conditions: vLLM on CMP 170HX, DeepSeek-V4-Flash with speculative decoding
quoted_support: Never. 8-10 tok/s, i.e. worse than no speculative decoding at all. CUDA graphs are worth ~12x.

claim: TP3 is arithmetically impossible for this checkpoint because 64 heads and 256 experts do not divide by 3, so topology choices are constrained by model shape as well as fabric.
stance_target: The repo's claim that TP is ruled out by the fabric - here it is also ruled out by divisibility
scope_conditions: DeepSeek-V4-Flash architecture on a 3-GPU or 5-GPU box
quoted_support: TP3 is also arithmetically impossible (64 heads, 256 experts don't divide by 3).

claim: DSpark speculative decoding is worth +1.93x decode over the same configuration without it, and unlike on TP it keeps winning under load.
stance_target: Whether speculative decoding is a viable throughput lever on this box
quoted_support: Worth +1.93x decode over the same config without it, and unlike on TP it keeps winning under load
